scenes.label: Meet the team
scenes.title: The Connection Lab
scenes.caption: Tara’s classroom helper correctly sorts four of six invented picture cards. Neel writes four successes on the display and leaves the other cards in a drawer. The teacher asks how a visitor could understand that report without knowing how many checks were attempted.
scenes.speech: Tara’s classroom helper correctly sorts four of six invented picture cards. Neel writes four successes on the display and leaves the other cards in a drawer. The teacher asks how a visitor could understand that report without knowing how many checks were attempted.

scenes.label: The problem
scenes.title: What changed?
scenes.caption: A useful mistake record keeps the checked label beside the prediction for every card. Agreement is a correct result; disagreement is an error to investigate. The total includes both kinds. Removing hard cases after seeing the outcome changes the story that the evidence tells.
scenes.speech: A useful mistake record keeps the checked label beside the prediction for every card. Agreement is a correct result; disagreement is an error to investigate. The total includes both kinds. Removing hard cases after seeing the outcome changes the story that the evidence tells.

scenes.label: How it works
scenes.title: Follow the evidence
scenes.caption: The team reports four correct and two incorrect out of six, then describes the mistaken cards. It proposes a new check rather than promising perfect future performance. Even a run with no mistakes would describe only the cases tested, not every possible drawing the helper might encounter.

scenes.label: Your decision
scenes.title: Decide and explain
scenes.caption: Six checks were run: four correct and two incorrect. Compare the actions, then explain which evidence supports your decision.
scenes.speech: Six checks were run: four correct and two incorrect. Compare the actions, then explain which evidence supports your decision.

scenes.label: What changes
scenes.title: Check the consequence
scenes.caption: Report four correct and two incorrect out of six, with the remaining limitations. A success count without the total hides relevant evidence.
scenes.speech: Report four correct and two incorrect out of six, with the remaining limitations. A success count without the total hides relevant evidence.
scenes.dialogue: Report correct, incorrect and total counts consistently.

scenes.label: Enter the lab
scenes.title: Investigate in the lab
scenes.caption: Investigate expected and predicted, then count every check, then report the limits. Test your plan, read feedback and try a changed case. Save evidence; explain one limitation.
scenes.speech: Investigate expected and predicted, then count every check, then report the limits. Test your plan, read feedback and try a changed case. Save evidence; explain one limitation.
scenes.dialogue: Why must a success count include how many checks were attempted?
